clinical_category: External ventricular drain infection prevention - minimizing unnecessary system manipulation
blueprint_topic: Prevention of healthcare-associated ventriculitis during CSF-drain management
stem: A nurse is caring for a client with an external ventricular drain (EVD) who has no clinical signs suggesting infection. Which action is most consistent with current IDSA guidance?

options.A: Avoid routine daily CSF cultures and analysis unless there is a clinical indication
options.B: Disconnect the drainage system every shift so the tubing can be cleaned internally
options.C: Replace the EVD at fixed intervals even when there is no infection or catheter malfunction
options.D: Continue systemic antimicrobial prophylaxis for the entire time the EVD remains in place

rationale: A is correct. The Infectious Diseases Society of America currently lists its healthcare-associated ventriculitis and meningitis guideline as CURRENT. For external CSF drains that are not being used to treat a CSF shunt infection, the guideline recommends against daily CSF cultures and analysis unless clinically indicated. IDSA also recommends against fixed-interval EVD exchange and against prolonged antimicrobial prophylaxis for the duration of an EVD. Unnecessary disconnection/manipulation can introduce microorganisms into the drainage system. B, C, and D therefore conflict with the current guideline or its infection-prevention rationale.
educational_objective: Reduce EVD-related infection risk by minimizing unnecessary CSF sampling and system manipulation and by avoiding routine fixed-interval exchange or prolonged antimicrobial prophylaxis when there is no clinical indication.
source_document_title: IDSA 2017 Clinical Practice Guidelines for Healthcare-Associated Ventriculitis and Meningitis
source_version_date: Published 2017-02-14; explicitly listed by IDSA as CURRENT at access 2026-08-18
source_locator: IDSA guideline → Section X, Recommendation 69: for external CSF drains not being used to treat CSF shunt infection, daily CSF cultures and analysis are not recommended unless clinically indicated. Section XII, Recommendations 76 and 78: prolonged antimicrobial prophylaxis for the duration of an EVD is not recommended; fixed-interval exchange of external ventricular drains is not recommended. Evidence summary: microorganisms may enter CSF drains through the drainage system, including through flushing/manipulation.
source_claim_supported: Current IDSA guidance directly supports avoiding routine daily CSF sampling, fixed-interval EVD exchange, and prolonged antimicrobial prophylaxis, while recognizing system manipulation as a route by which microorganisms may enter CSF drains.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control client-needs subcategory (10–16% of items); this item tests prevention of device-associated central nervous system infection and avoidance of unnecessary invasive-device manipulation.
correction_summary: Total clinical rebuild. The original generic AANN source asserted strict sterile technique for any ICP-device manipulation without an exact current locator and treated all ICP devices as equivalent. The final item narrows the construct to an external ventricular drain and uses a current IDSA guideline with exact recommendations on CSF sampling, fixed-interval exchange, prolonged prophylaxis, and infection risk from system manipulation.
audit_findings: The original AANN root URL did not provide an exact current locator for a universal sterile-technique rule across all ICP-monitoring devices.
IDSA currently labels the 2017 healthcare-associated ventriculitis and meningitis guideline as CURRENT.

The guideline directly recommends against routine daily CSF analysis/cultures in an external drain when not clinically indicated, against fixed-interval EVD exchange, and against prolonged antimicrobial prophylaxis for the duration of the drain.
The final item avoids overgeneralizing from external ventricular drains to every possible intracranial pressure-monitoring device.

Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely correct answer, no second defensible option, no unsupported sampling interval beyond the explicit guideline recommendation, no cueing, and no unresolved conflict.
